chapter_theme: Pattinathar's Nenjodu Magizhdal, rejoicing with the heart: where the Puranamalai confessed what the poet failed to know, this work tells the heart, verse by verse, what it has reached. The heart has loved the subtle that stood hidden in the body, become one with the awareness that fills everything, passed beyond speech, pointing, sky, earth, light, name, town, sex and number, and joined the Supreme as salt joins water, a river the sea, a crystal the colour set against it, sweetness the milk, vapour the water, and as the sun withdraws from the pots it shone in. The union is described only by negation and by figures of merging; nothing is said about how it was reached.
structure_note: The verses fall into two kinds that alternate. The negations (776 to 784, 794, 797) run a chain of இறந்து, 'having passed beyond', over pairs (before and after, sky and earth, space and light, town and name) and end in a verb of union (ஒன்றினையே, ஏகரித்தாய், சேர்ந்தனையே). The figures of union (789 to 793, 796) each give one simile. 785 to 788 and 795 to 800 name states: not male, female or neuter; sleeping without sleeping; the open expanse without liking and disliking; the fourth state; remaining as one is. Every verse ends in a second-person perfect addressed to நெஞ்சமே, the heart, and the poet never says 'I'.

776.reading: From that first day until today it has stood hidden in the body as the subtle; heart, you have come to love knowing that state.
776.nuance: அன்று முதல், from that day, is left undated: the day of birth, or the beginning of the world. The subtle (சூட்சியம்) is given no name, and the heart's achievement is only to have wanted to know it, which makes this verse the starting point of the sequence.

777.reading: In that which, as awareness here and as knowledge there, filled and became everything everywhere, heart, you were made one.
777.nuance: ஏகரித்தாய், you made one or became one, is the verb of union used again at 782. The pervading thing is described as உணர்வு and அறிவு, feeling-awareness and knowledge, not as a God; the work never names Siva.

778.reading: In the unmoving flood of great joy and bliss you stood firm, heart, having passed beyond form.
778.nuance: The flood (வெள்ளம்) does not move (அலையாத), which reverses the usual image of bliss as a torrent; the stability is the heart's and the flood's at once. உருவிறந்து, having gone past form, is the first of the chain of இறந்து that runs through the next verses.

779.reading: Without looking, without trembling, without drinking, without considering anything at all, heart, you became one with awareness.
779.nuance: Four negated verbs remove sight, agitation, consumption and inquiry, so that the union is with உணர்வு, bare awareness, from which the activities of knowing have been subtracted. The verse does not say that awareness is an object; the heart is one with it, not aware of it.

780.reading: Past theft and past killing, with things seen and the seeing itself gone, heart, you loved that which stands beyond measure.
780.nuance: The chain starts from the two gross sins, theft and killing, and passes at once to the end of object and perception (காண்பனவுங் காட்சியும்), so that the ladder from conduct to knowledge is a single line. A coded reading of களவு as the mind's thieving is possible but not needed.

781.reading: Past speech, past pointing, past after and past before, past the swimming, heart, you came to love that which stands.
781.nuance: சுட்டு is the demonstrative, the pointing by which a word indicates a thing, so the verse passes beyond both saying and indicating. நீச்சு, swimming, is read as the effort of crossing, the striving of practice, left behind once the far side is reached; it could also be a corrupt or variant form. 'After and before' are time, or the states before and after birth.

782.reading: Past sky, past earth, past space, past light and past thought, heart, you were made one with that which stands.
782.nuance: Space (வெளி) and light (ஒளி) are themselves the Siddhars' names for the goal, and the verse passes beyond them too; எண் is thought or number, and either way the countable is left. The pattern makes clear that nothing nameable is the end, including the words the Siddhars prefer.

783.reading: Wherever you looked, within and without, you took it as truth that it is the Supreme, strung through everything just as it is.
783.nuance: கோத்தபடி, as it is threaded, pictures the Supreme as the string through beads; உண்மையெனக் கொண்டனை, you took it as truth, is a conviction rather than a vision, the one verse in the work that describes the heart's attainment as a judgement.

784.reading: Past town and past name, past light and past space, past all distinction, heart, you joined that which stands.
784.nuance: ஊரும் பேரும், town and name, are the markers of a person's identity, and leaving them is the renunciant's act; here they are passed as the sky and light were. சீர், excellence or renown, is the last thing left. The verse repeats 782's light and space in reverse order, a mark of the kummi-like variation of one formula.

785.reading: Filled so that it is hard to call it male, female or neuter, and hard to see: that place, heart, you set your eye on.
785.nuance: The three grammatical genders are exhausted and the thing is beyond them; the verse does not say that it is a fourth, only that naming fails. காண அரிது, hard to see, is immediately followed by கண்ணுற்றாய், you saw it, so the difficulty is granted and overcome in one line.

786.reading: Putting away pride and fear, with knowledge, sleeping without sleeping, heart, you gained happiness.
786.nuance: தூங்காமல் தூங்கி, sleeping without sleeping, is read by tradition as the samadhi in which the body and senses rest as in sleep while awareness remains awake, the fourth state beyond deep sleep. The verse names ego and fear as the two things to remove first, and the sleep-that-is-not-sleep as what follows.

787.reading: The undivided all-fullness that stands as the First: heart, you reached the place where it is attained.
787.nuance: அகண்ட பரிபூரணம், the undivided plenum, is the Vedantic form of the Puranamalai's பூரணம். சாதியா நின்ற இடம் can be read as the place where it is attained (from சாதித்தல்) or as the place that stands without caste or kind (சாதி with the negative); the second would echo Pattinathar's listing of caste among the Fullness's creations (770), but the first is the simpler grammar.

788.reading: In the bare open expanse that has neither liking nor loathing, heart, you stayed, holding that simply to be there is happiness.
788.nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the bare expanse, is a Siddhar term for the ultimate as open space with nothing in it. The happiness is defined as இருப்பே, mere being there, with nothing done or gained, and the two attachments removed are the pair that drive action.

789.reading: Beyond and on this side of the great cosmos that no one reaches, heart, you gained a settled state like water and salt.
789.nuance: Water and salt is the Siddhars' figure for a union with no seam and no added bulk; the verse applies it to the heart's relation to what lies on both sides of the universe. ஆரும் உறா, that no one reaches, is said of the cosmic egg itself, so the heart is placed beyond what is already beyond reach.

790.reading: With the one who is hard to perceive though he is present with you, heart, you mingled like river water and the sea.
790.nuance: உடனாகவே இருந்தும், though he is right there with you, states the paradox the Puranamalai confessed (762): the nearest thing is the hardest to perceive. The river and the sea figure a union in which the smaller is lost in the greater and nothing comes back.

791.reading: Driving out the long-standing ego and cutting off the vice that stood in you, heart, you clung to it like a crystal to the colour set against it.
791.nuance: நெடியகம் is read as நெடிய அகம், the long-standing 'I'; it could also be the tall house, the body. படிகம், crystal, is the standard figure for the soul that shows the hue of whatever it is joined to, so the clinging is a taking-on of the other's nature rather than a grasp. சழக்கு is fault or wrongdoing. The syntax of படிகத்துக்கும் போல் is compressed and the simile is supplied from the tradition.

792.reading: To the Supreme that shines everywhere and above all, heart, you held as the sweetness that wells in milk holds to the milk.
792.nuance: The taste cannot be separated from the milk, so the figure is for a union of quality and substance rather than of two things. Pattinathar uses taste for union again at 773 (honey) and 804 (toddy).

793.reading: As cool vapour parts from water and becomes water again, heart, you became one with the one who has no town and no name.
793.nuance: The figure grants a separation before the return: vapour was water, left it and becomes water again, so the soul came from and goes back to the One rather than joining a stranger. ஊரொடு பேரில்லான், the one with no town and no name, is what the heart itself became in 784, so the two are alike before they merge.

794.reading: Laying this birth waste so as to remain just as you are, heart, you reached the place that is hard to tell.
794.nuance: இருந்தபடியே இருக்க, to remain as one is, is the phrase for the natural or settled state in which nothing further is done; it recurs at 800. பாழ்படுத்தி, laying waste, is said of the birth, not the body: the life as a career is what is emptied.

795.reading: Leaving behind all the higher states one after another, examining, heart, you walked in the fourth state.
795.nuance: பதம் is a state or station. On one reading the fourth is turiya, beyond waking, dream and deep sleep, and the higher states left behind are those three; on another the fourth is sayujya, the union that follows the three graded releases (salokam, samipam, sarupam), which are then the 'higher states' given up. The verb நடந்தனை, you walked, makes the fourth a ground one moves on rather than a point reached.

796.reading: Knowing the place into which the sun that plays in pot after pot withdraws, heart, you came to love it.
796.nuance: The sun reflected in many pots of water is the stock figure for the one Self appearing as many; the verse adds அடங்கும் இடம், the place where the sun itself withdraws or is contained, so the heart's knowledge is of the source rather than of the reflections. ஊடாடி, playing through, treats the many appearances as the sun's own sport.

797.reading: In that which stands as the learned one, the hearer, the unseen one, the seer and the one near at hand, heart, you became one.
797.nuance: The list makes the one thing stand as every party to knowing: the one who learned, the one who heard, the one who is not seen, the one who sees, the one who is present. Learning and hearing are the Kural's two roads to knowledge, and here they are forms the One takes rather than means to it.

798.reading: Where the four inner instruments and the five senses they govern become one and stand composed, heart, you joined.
798.nuance: நாலுவகைக் கரணம் are the four inner instruments (mind, intellect, will and ego) of the tattva scheme; நல்கு புலனைந்து are the five senses they give rise to or direct. The nine are not destroyed but made one and steadied (சீலமுற்று), which keeps the body's apparatus inside the union.

799.reading: What is let go and what is touched, the place of the sky and the place of the earth: heart, you saw them as one nature that holds them all.
799.nuance: கட்டும் ஒரு தன்மை, one nature that binds, is the thread image of 783 again; the first pair, விட்டிடமும் தொட்டிடமும், the left and the touched, covers everything the heart has renounced and everything it still handles, so renunciation itself is placed inside the one nature.

800.reading: So as to remain, on every day whatever, just as you are, heart, you made that into a state beyond happiness.
800.nuance: சுகாதீதம், beyond sukha, places the final state past even the happiness named in 786 and 788, as the Tirumanthiram's அதீதம் lies past turiya; or it is the beyond that is itself happiness. The condition is the same as 794's, remaining as one is, and the verse closes the first run with it.

links.note: Tirumular's light within the dark is neither woman nor man nor neuter and cannot be known by anyone; Pattinathar's place is filled so that it is hard to call it male, female or neuter and hard to see. Both exhaust the three genders and both pass from unknowability to a knowing of it, Tirumular by searching out the Lord's greatness, Pattinathar by the heart's eye.

Tirumular's Siva-yogis, with turiya risen in waking, bonds cut and senses and life made one, remain with the body as if dead; Pattinathar's heart sleeps without sleeping and gains happiness. The state is the same, a sleep-like stillness in which awareness stays awake, and Pattinathar names what is removed first, pride and fear.

Sivavakkiyar makes a measure of water and a measure of salt one measure to say that Vishnu and Siva are one; Pattinathar uses water and salt for the heart's settled state on both sides of the cosmos. The same figure of a seamless union serves there for the identity of two gods and here for the identity of the heart with what is beyond the world.

Tirumular: as whiteness changes when red stands before it, so the soul coming within the Supreme becomes the flag joined to the red Siva-Meru; Pattinathar's heart clings to the Supreme as a crystal to the colour set against it. Both make the soul colourless in itself and coloured by what it joins, and both use the figure for the union itself rather than for a stage before it.

Tirumular says those who have left the evil path and are flawless in the fourth state become Him, and calls this sanmarga; Pattinathar's heart leaves the higher states one by one, examines, and walks in the fourth. On the turiya reading of both, the fourth state is the ground on which one becomes the Supreme, and both place it after an examination that rejects what came before.

Sivavakkiyar says the cause stands beyond the beyond, past Hari, Brahma and the three colours, 'beyond even turiya, far, far, far', and tells the hearer to hold to that; Pattinathar's heart walks in the fourth state as its attainment. If Pattinathar's fourth is turiya, the two verses place the goal on different sides of the fourth state; if his fourth is sayujya, the fourth of the releases, there is no conflict, since that lies past the states of consciousness altogether.

Tirumular: when the sun appears in pot after pot, closing the pots does not shut him in, and so the Lord in the body is not confined by it. Pattinathar: the heart knows the place into which the sun that plays in pot after pot withdraws. The figure is the same, one sun in many waters; Tirumular uses it for the Lord's freedom from the body, Pattinathar for the heart's finding of the source behind the reflections.

Tirumular says that once the five senses, their five objects and the four inner instruments are understood together, the soul becomes as it was of old and abides spread out as the whole; Pattinathar's heart joins where the four inner instruments and the five senses become one and stand composed. Both keep the tattva apparatus within the union, made one rather than cast off.

source_issues: 776 to 800 are printed without word spaces, while 801 to 807 (the next chapter) have spaces before the refrain and, in 805, between words; the two runs appear to come from differently prepared sources.
781 line 2, நீச்சிறந்து, is doubtful: நீச்சு (swimming) fits the chain of இறந்து but may be a variant or corrupt word.
